15ecnlt.en: <1>None.</1> Shield Force does not collect, receive, store on a server, or transmit any personal or sensitive information about you. It has no backend server, no user accounts, no sign-in, and no analytics, advertising, tracking or crash-reporting software of any kind. The app runs entirely as code on your device.

1l0k4mh.en: <1>Shield Force does not operate a database, and does not need one.</1> The app is a set of static files. Nothing you enter is ever sent to a server, there is no place where user records could be written, and no account system to create a record in the first place. We hold no user table, no message log, no quiz history and no contact list.

rt6xup.en: You never register, sign in, or provide a name, phone number, email address, service number, PPO number, rank, unit or bank detail anywhere in this app — nothing asks for them, because there is nowhere to put them.

17fdyeo.en: This has a practical consequence worth stating plainly: <1>there is no store of user data here that could be breached, sold, subpoenaed, or leaked</1>, because it does not exist. We cannot hand over information about you to anyone, including ourselves.

3rk77x.en: Shield Force does <1>not</1> read, collect or use any device identifier — not the IMEI, IMSI, SIM serial number, phone number, Android ID, advertising ID (AAID/IDFA), MAC address or any other identifier — and does not fingerprint your device. It does not access your location, contacts, call logs, SMS, photos, camera or microphone. Because it collects no identifiers and no personal data, it never links one to another.

16na27h.en: When you paste a message into the <1>message scanner</1>, that text is checked entirely on your own device against a built-in list of fraud patterns. The scanner is a set of rules inside the app; it does <2>not</2> use any third-party or online AI service. <3>The message is never uploaded, logged, stored or sent anywhere</3> — it is discarded the moment you leave the screen or clear the field.

xhvw2h.en: A small amount of information is saved in the app's local storage on your device, purely so the app remembers your progress and settings between visits. It is never sent to us or anyone else and is not visible to us. The only copy that can exist elsewhere is inside your phone's own encrypted device backup (iCloud or Google), if you have backups switched on:

s6irvs.en: <1>Training scores</1> — your best result on each quiz module, so progress isn't lost.

wst80h.en: <1>App settings</1> — such as that you have accepted the terms, your language choice, and whether you've dismissed a banner.

yvomvx.en: We do <1>not</1> share, sell, rent, trade or disclose any user data to anyone — no advertisers, data brokers, analytics or AI companies, partners or government bodies — because we do not have any. There are no categories of third parties with whom we share user data.

szm8wc.en: The store apps are built with <1>Capacitor</1>, an open-source app framework, together with the standard Android and Apple system components. qa0dmt.en: On the website, Shield Force installs a service worker so pages, images and the downloadable PDF reports keep working without an internet connection after your first visit. This is a standard web technology for offline apps and does not collect or transmit any data about you.

1rpuy84.en: <1>The app-store versions</1> of Shield Force carry every screen inside the app on your device, so nothing about you is sent anywhere when you use them.

1s4x9pc.en: <1>If you use Shield Force as a website</1>, the company that hosts it (Netlify) receives the standard technical details that every website visit involves — such as your IP address, browser type and the page requested — in order to deliver the pages and protect against abuse. 1ujq05.en: Google and Apple may provide us with anonymous, aggregated statistics such as total downloads. These are produced by the stores under their own privacy policies, not by the app, and contain no personal data.

h9wqjj.en: The best protection for personal data is not to collect it, which is how Shield Force is built. What the app saves stays in its private storage on your device, protected by your phone's own security (screen lock and encryption). The website is served only over encrypted HTTPS.

1h0tyu8.en: You list a sofa, bike or car on OLX-type apps. A polite 'Army officer under posting' agrees to full price instantly — no bargaining, no inspection.

lwj0qe.en: You enter your account number, PAN, Aadhaar and net-banking password on the fake page.

h3ce1m.en: A 'verification OTP' arrives — it is actually the transaction OTP for a transfer or SIM swap the fraudster just initiated.
